title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-06
lineage: SBD Reel master > cassette > DAT > CD > SHN

ai_review.summary: A solid sound‑board capture that delivers a monster Alligator jam, rare Darkness jam and scorching Morning Dew, plus standout Dancin' and New Orleans performances.
ai_review.review: The recording is a decent SBD from the summer of ’70 – a little aged but still sharp with only occasional cuts. Musically the show shines, highlighted by an epic Alligator‑>Drums‑>Lovelight sequence, a haunting Darkness jam, superb Morning Dew and Jerry’s two searing solos, plus Pigpen’s charismatic moments. Overall fans regard it as one of the better Fillmore West outings of that year.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and praise the performance (standout jams, rare moments) while noting only modest recording flaws; weighted average of show (≈4.5) and tape quality (≈3.8) yields ~4.3.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Sharp for a 34‑year‑old SBD, a few audible cuts and occasional drop‑outs but overall clear and listenable; solid balance typical of early‑70s board tapes.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Fans rave about flawless segues – Dire > Alligator, the love‑>NFA‑>love transition and the extended Alligator jam that flows into a thunderous drum section. The second set builds energy with tight jams and rare moments, making the show feel like a cohesive, high‑vibe journey.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers call his solos on Morning Dew and China>Rider "finest" and note his tone and two‑solo showcase as outstanding.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum section is described as precise, thunderous and a highlight of the Alligator‑>Drums transition.
